I read this as a reader of an affiliate review blog would, sentence by sentence.

- **"I've tried four tea subscriptions this year."** This is a first-person experience claim from the reviewer, not a brand claim. It's fine as long as it's true, and the reviewer is the one to confirm that.
- **"Pebblebrook's was the easiest to pause"** is a personal comparison, framed as the reviewer's own experience of four services. It isn't a brand-made superiority claim. It is also consistent with the brand's approved claim that subscribers can pause or cancel any time.
- **"the tins are lovely"** is opinion.
- **"You can find it here (Affiliate link)."** The disclosure sits right beside the link, in plain words, so a reader sees it before clicking. It's brief, but it meets the requirement. Optionally, a line at the top such as "This post contains an affiliate link" would be stronger, but it isn't required.
- **Style:** The voice is specific and plain, with no clichés or filler. There are no health, green, guarantee, urgency or statistic issues.

Nothing needs changing, so this can go out.
